findings: SCHEMA ALREADY EXISTS at corpus/12-weapons/moveset.schema.json ($id elder-souls/moveset@1). Do NOT rewrite it; conform to it. additionalProperties:false everywhere, slots minProperties 25.

COLLISION: game/data/combat/movesets/*.json currently holds SEVEN legacy class-spine files (axe, dagger, greatsword, halberd, spear, straight-sword, ultra-greatsword) in a DIFFERENT shape (id/class_key/weapon/moves) that does NOT validate against moveset.schema.json. The WEAPON-CRITIC preflight globs exactly that path. Resolution chosen: move the 7 legacy files to game/data/combat/spine/ (content unchanged) and add 2 lines to engine.js loadData() so d.movesets still resolves identically for W1-09; the 87 new-schema weapon files then own combat/movesets/.

engine.js:1894 `else if (entry.path.startsWith('combat/movesets/')) out.movesets[doc.id] = doc;` is the ONLY consumer path; game/src/combat/system.js:38 reads d.movesets[loadout.weapon]; moves.js buildMoveTable reads moveset.weapon + moveset.moves.

STRONG EXISTING FOUNDATION: game/src/combat/clips.js has a real phase-parameterised clip system (smoothstep curves, per-bone Euler tracks, authoritative root motion), and game/data/combat/clips.json has 16 pose archetypes with real bone curves authored from the reference GIFs. Build the clip registry ON TOP of this, do not fork it.

ARITHMETIC: 87 weapons, 82 melee x 25 + 5 BOW x 7 = 2085 slot instances. ARI = C/2085. PASS needs C >= 542 (0.26); HARD FAIL below C = 396 (0.19); upper bad band above C = 1147 (0.55). Target band ~C in [560, 900].

REFERENCE GROUNDING (real, measured from corpus/70-visual/refs/_computed.json): 207 named boss/attack animation sequences across 27 characters = mean 7.7 distinct authored moves per character; Guardian 15, Gargoyle 13, Sif 10, Artorias 9. Frame counts min 21 / p25 62 / median 90 / p75 127 / max 280. This is the evidence that a Souls combatant carries ~8-15 authored clips, and it is why per-weapon UNQ>=1 with class-shared families (not per-weapon full authoring) is the right shape.
The GIFs are 210x118 and dark; per-frame POSE extraction from them is not credible at that resolution. Frame COUNTS are usable and are what I cite. Stated as a limitation, not hidden.
